Brompton.hq: Greenford, London, UK (a new Ashford, Kent headquarters has been announced)
Brompton.ownership: Private. A 15% stake was sold in June 2026 (per Wikipedia).
Brompton.positioning: Folding bikes for city commuting, built in London, with a growing electric range.
Brompton.dataNote: Founding year: Wikipedia gives June 1976 for the company; other sources say 1975 (the bike's design). Headcount is a Revelio Labs estimate, not a company figure.

Tern.ownership: Privately held. Founded by Joshua Hon and Florence Shen, who are connected to Dahon's founding family.
Tern.positioning: Folding, cargo and electric bikes for everyday urban transport.
Tern.dataNote: Wikipedia says its products are sold in 65 countries. No country list was found, so the map is not filled in.

Dahon.hq: Offices in the US, Europe and China
Dahon.ownership: Founded by Dr David T. Hon, who is still CEO per Wikipedia.
Dahon.positioning: Folding bikes; says it ranked first in folding-bike retail volume in mainland China and globally in 2023 (its own claim, citing a CIC report).
Dahon.dataNote: Dahon's own pages quote different country counts (28+, 40+ and 70+). No country list was found, so the map is not filled in.

Ahooga.positioning: Belgian-designed and built 20-inch folding bike (A-MAX) with a patented hinge-free double-triangle frame, upgradeable to electric (E-MAX).
Ahooga.dataNote: Belgian design and manufacture per BIKE Magazin. No founding year, headcount or country list found.

Gocycle.positioning: Premium folding e-bike with a proprietary front-hub motor, single-sided carbon fork and 10-second fold.
Gocycle.dataNote: Press describes Gocycle as made by Karbon Kinetics. Headquarters, founding year and headcount were not confirmed.

Birdy.positioning: Full-suspension folding bike designed by Riese & Müller and built by Pacific Cycles in Taiwan.
Birdy.dataNote: CHECK: Wikipedia says Riese & Müller stopped marketing and selling the Birdy in 2025 to focus on e-bikes. Confirm whether the Birdy is still sold (for example by Pacific Cycles) before treating it as an active competitor.
